Pairwise comparison of generated summaries or rationale sets according to the listed criteria

We ask annotators to compare the two types of summaries in a pairwise manner based on four criteria: which summary includes more information (informativeness), which summary contains less repeated phrases (non-redundancy), which summary is easier to read (coherence), and which summary is more useful for decision making (usefulness).

changes_made.explanation: Consolidated guideline descriptions and removed redundant/repetitive text. All extracted criteria were accurate and appropriate.

overall_notes: The extraction was generally accurate. The paper presents a novel approach to opinion summarization (RATION) that generates representative opinions with supporting rationales. Key observations: (1) The paper clearly addresses NLG (opinion summarization), (2) Uses both automatic metrics and human evaluation extensively, (3) Does NOT use LLMs as judges (only as baseline generators), (4) Conducts thorough human evaluation via Amazon Mechanical Turk. The main improvements needed were normalization of names and removing redundant/duplicate items.
